questions.0.explain.t: The right key (account, token, ASN, combinations) separates abuse from legitimate use better.

questions.0.options.0.t: NAT groups many legitimate users, and botnets spread traffic across many IPs

questions.0.options.1.t: IP addresses do not appear in the HTTP request logs

questions.0.options.2.t: A per-IP limit is banned by law in some countries

questions.0.options.3.t: IPv6 cannot be limited by most tools

questions.0.q.t: Why is limiting only by IP often insufficient?

questions.1.explain.t: Challenge, short block and then longer: proportional and reversible.

questions.1.options.0.t: So a misclassification does not become a permanent block and the response grows with repeat offenses

questions.1.options.1.t: To save storage for block logs

questions.1.options.2.t: To avoid using challenges, which annoy users

questions.1.options.3.t: Because blocks with no expiry are technically impossible to apply

questions.1.q.t: Why use a response ladder with an expiry (TTL)?

questions.2.explain.t: Campaigns and seasonality change what is normal; the baseline follows. The static ceiling remains as a safeguard.

questions.2.options.0.t: It follows the normal behavior of each endpoint and window, instead of a fixed number that goes stale

questions.2.options.1.t: It removes the need to keep any static limit

questions.2.options.2.t: It removes the need for telemetry, because it adjusts by itself

questions.2.options.3.t: It guarantees there will never be a false positive

questions.2.q.t: What is the advantage of an adaptive limit?
